sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Cu–Zn binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset CuZn-08Gie.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, (Cu) + L → β, lies at 899 °C.
The Cu–Zn system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as peritectic, intermetallic rich, order disorder.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of W. Gierlotka, S.-W. Chen, J. Mater. Res., 23, 258-63(2008). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
For Cu, the liquidus meets the axis at 1085 °C.
Pure Zn melts at 420 °C.
The peritectic reaction (Cu) + L → β is calculated at 899 °C, with L at x(Zn) = 0.375.
We obtain 834 °C for the peritectic reaction (β + L → γ), where L has a mole fraction of 0.593.
The dataset places a peritectic (γ + L → δ) at 703 °C; the composition of L is a mole fraction of 0.804.
We obtain 600 °C for the peritectic reaction (δ + L → ε), where L has x(Zn) = 0.883.
The dataset places a eutectoid (δ → γ + ε) at 559 °C; the composition of δ is a mole fraction of 0.749.
The dataset places a peritectoid (β + γ → β′) at 463 °C; the composition of β′ is a mole fraction of 0.491.
Eutectoid equilibrium β → (Cu) + β′ is found at 460 °C and a mole fraction of 0.445 (β).
The eutectic reaction L → ε + (Zn) is calculated at 419 °C, with L at x(Zn) = 0.980.
β′ is stable up to 463 °C.
The solubility of Cu in (Zn) reaches a mole fraction of 0.019 at 419 °C.
At 1450 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −6436 J/mol, at x(Zn) = 0.440.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of δ at 298.15 K is −5.76 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
Its heat capacity at room temperature is 25.16 J/(mol K).
For the equiatomic liquid at 1450 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −14.55 kJ/mol-atom.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
